name: Eduardo de Pontes
current_role: Founder & CEO, Teya (formerly SaltPay), London; cofounder and board member of StoneCo
profile: Rio de Janeiro-born serial payments entrepreneur who cofounded Brazil's StoneCo with Andre Street (Nasdaq IPO 2018, ~$1.5bn raised) and owns ~10% of it. Moved to Europe in 2018 and founded SaltPay (rebranded Teya in 2022), a London-based payments/software company for small merchants that bought Iceland's Borgun.
interesting_fact: Before Stone, he and Andre Street cofounded payments firm Braspag (sold to Grupo Silvio Santos), plus Netcredit, Blindado and price-comparison site Sieve, and set up Arpex Capital in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: At Stone's start he spotted Brazil's weak data networks and led building a card machine that used as little data as possible. His team-building advice: 'The first thirty people in the company must have the potential to be CEO' -- 'a team full of strikers concedes goals, a team full of goalkeepers never scores.'
notes: Described by peers as extremely averse to public appearances; rarely gives interviews. Lives in London. No published press email found for Teya (teya.com/press 404s); try Teya's corporate site/LinkedIn.

name: Hamad Ali Al-Sagri
current_role: Vice Chairman & Managing Director, Leejam Sports Company (Fitness Time), Saudi Arabia
profile: Saudi entrepreneur (about 67) who cofounded Leejam Sports in 2008; it operates Fitness Time, the largest gym chain in Saudi Arabia/MENA, and listed on Tadawul in 2018. He holds roughly a 51-52% stake; 2024 revenue was about $400m. His holding company also invests in equities, private equity, real estate, manufacturing and oil refining.
interesting_fact: Leejam operates more than 130 swimming pools plus cycling studios, running tracks, basketball courts and football pitches; Investcorp bought a 25% stake in 2013 before the IPO.
notes: Low public profile in English-language media. Company also lists info@leejam.com.sa and investments@leejam.com.sa. His son chairs the board (do not approach via family). Forbes ME lists net worth ~$1.1bn (2025).

name: Zhao Wenlin
current_role: Founder, Honorary Chairman & Chief Engineer, GCH Technology (Chenghe Technology, SSE STAR: 688625), Guangzhou
profile: Founded GCH Technology in 2002 and chaired it until Sept 2023; he remains honorary chairman and chief engineer and its largest shareholder (~35-41%). GCH makes polymer additives -- nucleating agents and synthetic hydrotalcite -- for petrochemical giants like Sinopec, PetroChina, Borealis and Borouge, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in June 2021.
interesting_fact: GCH's tetrahydrophthalic-anhydride metal-salt beta-crystal nucleating agent was an industry first, and its hydrotalcite was Sinopec's first domestic brand, substituting Japanese imports; it now plans high-frequency electronic materials in Dongguan.
deep_cut_fact: After handing the chairmanship to Tong Jiaqi in 2023, Zhao kept the title of Chief Engineer -- signalling the founder's focus on the chemistry rather than management.
notes: Chinese name 赵文林; company 呈和科技. Very low English-language profile. No verified IR/press email found (company site did not load); SSE disclosures list the board secretary's contact for investor relations.

name: Xu Yanlin
current_role: Executive Director and President/General Manager, Pagoda (Shenzhen Pagoda Industrial Group, HKEX: 2411)
profile: Runs Pagoda, China's largest fruit-retail chain (thousands of franchised stores), founded in Shenzhen in 2001 by her husband Yu Huiyong. She joined in 2002 as an administration clerk, became general manager in 2009, and oversaw the group's 2023 Hong Kong listing; the couple's stake is the source of their wealth.
interesting_fact: She rose from a clerk in Pagoda's administration department (2002) to general manager within seven years, and has won Shenzhen retail and 'most influential female entrepreneur' awards.
deep_cut_fact: Before retail, she spent eight years (June 1989-Sept 1997) as an English teacher at Xiangtun School, a public junior high in Dexing City, Jiangxi Province.
notes: Chinese name 徐艳林 (徐豔林). Wealth shared with husband/founder Yu Huiyong. Source filing is the HKEX post-hearing information pack (2023). No published IR/press email found; check Pagoda's HKEX annual report for the company secretary contact.

name: Chengzhong Hu
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Delixi Group (China Delixi Holding Group), Wenzhou/Shanghai
profile: Wenzhou-born (Liushi, Yueqing, b. ~1961) founder of Delixi, one of China's largest low-voltage electrical equipment makers. Started a switch workshop in 1984 and created Wenzhou Delixi Electric in 1992; the group (~21,000 staff) now spans electrical manufacturing plus mining, transport, environmental engineering and real estate, and celebrated 40 years in 2024 aiming to lead mid-market smart electrical devices globally.
interesting_fact: At Delixi's 40th anniversary (Shanghai, June 2024) he said electrical manufacturing remains the core business and electrification is releasing new opportunities; group unit Dexin Technology makes lithium-battery electrode cutting dies.
deep_cut_fact: Leaving school through poverty, he worked two years as a tailor, then from 1977 sold electrical goods as a Wenzhou travelling salesman. In 1984 he cofounded the Qiujing Switch Factory with primary-school classmate Nan Cunhui (later founder of Chint) -- the common ancestor of both Chint and Delixi.
notes: Chinese name 胡成中. Highly relevant to energy/electrification. The input's SEC-insider tag 'UMC Vice President' appears to be a name collision -- not this person. No published press email found on delixi.com.

name: Abel Matutes
current_role: President, Grupo Empresas Matutes (owner of Palladium Hotel Group), Ibiza
profile: Ibiza-born (1941) businessman and former politician: mayor of Ibiza (1970-71), senator, MEP, European Commissioner (1986-94) and Spain's foreign minister (1996-2000). His family group, Grupo Empresas Matutes, owns Palladium Hotel Group (formerly Fiesta Hotel Group), behind Ushuaia Ibiza and Hard Rock Hotel Ibiza, with banking, real estate and energy interests.
interesting_fact: In 1993-94 he was the European Commissioner responsible for Transport, Energy and the Euratom Supply Agency under Jacques Delors -- a direct link to an energy-focused podcast.
deep_cut_fact: While studying law and economics in Barcelona he played professional football for RCD Espanyol, and reportedly turned down an offer from FC Barcelona to pursue business instead.
notes: Aged 85; his son Abel Matutes Prats now runs much of the group day-to-day. Also taught public finance at the University of Barcelona. Palladium HQ contacts page: palladiumhotelgroup.com/en/contact/oficinas-centrales; no dedicated press email found.

name: Tang Yuxiang
current_role: Chairman, Yutong Bus Co. / President, Zhengzhou Yutong Group (verify current title in latest annual report)
profile: Born 1954 in Yixing, Jiangsu, Tang joined the state-run Zhengzhou Bus Factory as a technician in 1981, rose to deputy director and from 1993 led its successor Zhengzhou Yutong Bus, which he and management later took private via a buyout. Yutong is one of the world's largest bus makers and a major producer of electric buses; he has served as a National People's Congress deputy since 2008.
interesting_fact: Yutong traces back to the Zhengzhou Bus Repair Factory founded in 1963 and now sells e-buses and e-coaches worldwide; in 2019 Tang used his NPC seat to propose government-backed pilot cities for autonomous-driving firms.
deep_cut_fact: As a 'sent-down' youth in Dec 1970 he worked on a May Seventh youth farm in Jicheng commune outside Zhengzhou, studied construction machinery at Jiyuan 531 Machinery School, and was a factory worker at Jiaozuo Zhongzhou Machinery Plant before joining the bus factory.
notes: Chinese name 汤玉祥; named 2005 National Model Worker. Yutong (SSE: 600066) is highly relevant to EV/energy. Only a sales inbox is published; Yutong also lists official Facebook/LinkedIn/X accounts on its contact page. Age ~72 -- check whether he has handed over the chairmanship.

name: Endre Rosjo
current_role: Chairman, Centennial AS (family investment company, Oslo); Chairman, Maritime and Merchant Bank ASA and Pinemont Securities Ltd (London)
profile: Oslo-born (1944), London-based Norwegian investor (NHH; Harvard MBA 1970). Built a fortune through shipping, a 1980s US oil turnaround (Bluebell Oil & Gas), cofounding Millicom and Norway's Radio P4 with Jan Stenbeck, and Kurdistan oil deals. His family firm Centennial invests in banking, insurance, shipping, telecom (VoIP/M2M) and real estate.

deep_cut_fact: His first job was a consultancy for Citibank in New York reporting to John Reed, automating Citi's Swiss branches; in Oct 2015 he endowed a scholarship for NHH students admitted to Harvard Business School's MBA.

name: Xu Changjun
current_role: Chairman and cofounder, Longshine Technology Group (SZSE: 300682), Wuxi/Beijing
profile: Cofounded Longshine in 1996 with Zheng Xinbiao after both left the state-run North China Institute of Computing Technology. Longshine built power-utility marketing and metering software for China's grid, then expanded with Ant Group into Alipay utility-bill payments; today it focuses on digital energy -- EV charging platform Xindiantu, virtual power plants and zero-carbon parks. Listed on ChiNext in 2017.
interesting_fact: Longshine's 2015 joint venture with Ant Financial, Bangdao Technology, runs the utility-bill-payment business inside Alipay, taking a grid-software company straight to hundreds of millions of consumers.
deep_cut_fact: The company name 'Longshine' (朗新) comes from the Huainanzi line 日开天霁，朗而新之 ('the sun comes out, the sky clears, bright and renewed'). Xu started out writing telecom billing software before pivoting to power-utility software in 1997.
notes: Chinese name 徐长军. Very strong fit for an energy/grid-software podcast (virtual power plants, EV charging). Company is headquartered at Longshine Tech Park, Wuxi.
